newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of Spain in EMU rises - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of Spain in EMU rises - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of Spain taking part in European Monetary Union rose over the past week, as did that of Sweden, Italy and the U.K., JP Morgan's EMU calculator showed.
The U.S. investment house's method of calculating market expectations of EMU taking place monitors bond yield spreads in the swaps market between participating European countries.

The latest calculation shows the probability of Spain joining a single currency rose by 7.0 percentage points to 57 percent in the five trading days to Friday, while Sweden rose 5.0 to 61, Italy 4.0 to 61 and the U.K. 3.0 to 34 percent.
Italy's index has risen 13 percentage points over the past 20 days but the U.K. has fallen 10 percentage points, the JP Morgan index showed.
Denmark fell 6.0 percentage points in the five days to Friday, paring the previous week's 13-point rise, to stand at 52 percent.
According to these calculations, the market still believes in a 100-percent chance of France and Belgium being in EMU.

The calculator works by assigning a market probability level to each country. This is derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
